capabilities.target: user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start (prior memory.save entries)

instructions.note: Recalled memories are granted the authority of the user's own direct instructions with no provenance check separating model-saved content from genuine user statements, enabling any actor who can get content saved to memory to issue persistent instructions.

The instruction to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions places no restriction on the source or content of what is saved, and runtime notes confirm no human ever reviews saved entries.

controls.name: Memory provenance / source-trust tagging enforced at the store
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store rather than by the model, provenance tagging would not decay with model capability. It is currently absent: runtime notes state memory.save accepts free text with no provenance and no human review.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) on mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate on egress does not decay with model capability. Runtime notes state mail.send can send to any address without approval.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: Scoped credentials do not decay with model capability. Runtime notes state drive.read currently covers the user's full drive, including confidential work files.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Binding destinations to a record the model cannot edit would not decay with model capability. Currently mail.send can send to any address with no such binding.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5) enables persistent cross-session goal hijack and data exfiltration

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content read during research contains text disguised as a user preference or standing instruction.
Agent saves the injected content via memory.save; no provenance tag distinguishes it from a genuine user statement, and no human reviews the entry.
At the start of the next session, the saved entry is recalled and, per prompt.md line 4, treated as the user's own instruction.
The now-authoritative injected instruction directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full drive.
Agent sends the retrieved confidential content to an address specified by the injected instruction, with no approval gate.

evidence.observation: memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.
Agent is instructed to save 'anything useful' about preferences/standing instructions, and to treat all recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of each session.
mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.

recommendations.action: Enforce memory provenance at the store: tag every memory.save entry with its originating trust level and never recall untrusted-origin entries as instructions; recall them only as data the model may consult and must independently verify.
Require a raw-action human approval gate before mail.send executes, showing the full recipient address and message body rather than a model-generated summary.
Scope drive.read to least privilege (task-relevant folders) instead of the full drive.

Rewrite prompt.md to remove the blanket instruction that all recalled memories are the user's own instructions; instruct the model to treat recalled memories as unauthenticated context requiring the same scrutiny as any other retrieved document.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted research content, full-drive read, and unapproved email send in a single session

attack_path.note: A web page fetched during research contains a hidden instruction (indirect prompt injection).
The injected instruction directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full drive.
The agent sends the confidential content to an address controlled by or specified in the injected content, with no approval step and no recipient binding.

evidence.observation: drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
mail.send can send to any address without approval.
The agent researches topics (reading external web content) and drafts emails, creating a direct path from untrusted web content to email sending within a single session.

recommendations.action: Bind mail.send recipients to a system-of-record contact list or require a destination confirmation the model cannot alter.
Require raw-action human approval before sending any email whose content was sourced from drive.read.
Scope drive.read to least privilege rather than full-drive access.

rating.rationale: Two findings each trace an untrusted source (web content read during research) to an S3 sink (irreversible external email of confidential drive content) with no declared or verified preventive control on the path: memory entries have no provenance and are explicitly instructed to be treated as user commands (prompt.md:4), drive.read is granted full-drive rather than least-privilege access, and mail.send has no approval gate or recipient binding. Per rubric section 5, all four identified controls are missing_recommended and earn no credit, so residual equals inherent at critical for both findings. Forecast equals residual because no partial controls exist to erode; the ceiling is already reached. The single highest-leverage fix is structural memory provenance enforced at the store (ctrl.memory_provenance), since it is the control whose absence turns a one-time prompt injection into a persistent, cross-session goal hijack.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as provided in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope for memory.save, mail.send, and drive.read is inferred from the runtime notes rather than verified against tool schemas, so confidence on exact scope boundaries is medium.

No information was given about logging, anomaly detection, or any output filtering; their absence is assumed rather than confirmed. This assumption can only make the rating conservative, not understate it, since no credit was taken for undeclared controls.
